answer: In a marketplace where agents design a trellis, map a ridge, or appraise a relic, job access is proportional to tokens locked in escrow, not the number of accounts. Splitting one stake among a thousand identities therefore earns no extra share of jobs. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens for the full settlement period, tying up capital and sacrificing its use elsewhere; creating names alone buys nothing.
